title: Inference KPI proto schema versioning and compatibility gateway
creator: Diego Morales
description: Problem: As we onboard more model variants and cross-region collectors, metric envelopes (OTel & Prometheus adapters) diverge in field names and labeling. Upstream changes (new labels, renamed fields, optional typed values) cause downstream consumers and rollups to either drop signals or misattribute metrics. We need a single compatibility gateway that validates, versions, and normalizes incoming inference KPI envelopes before they enter the ingestion mesh.
detailed_scope: Build a small compatibility service that: 1) maintains a registry of protobuf/JSON schema versions for inference KPI envelopes; 2) validates incoming OTLP/Prometheus metric batches against the registry; 3) performs safe, well-defined transformations for tolerated changes (rename maps, defaulting, type coercion where safe); 4) emits a normalized internal envelope with a wire_version header; 5) records validation regressions and exposes per-tenant validation metrics; 6) supports a canary mode to opt-in tenants to stricter validation and migration guidance.
design_decisions:
- Use protobuf schema registry (git-backed with signed commits) so schema changes are auditable.
- Non-breaking changes are allowed without gating (e.g., adding optional label). Breaking changes require a new schema version and a migration plan.
- Implement a policy layer with rules: rename mappings, allowed coercions, and blacklisted fields. Rules are versioned.
- Integrate with existing OTLP adapter: compatibility gateway runs as a filter in the ingest path for Prom/OTLP agents.
- Failures: metric validation failures are not dropped by default — they are tagged and forwarded to a low-priority dead-letter pipeline for investigation, with a configurable policy to reject when in strict mode.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility gateway validates OTLP and Prometheus envelopes against the registered schema and emits a normalized internal envelope with wire_version metadata.
There is tooling to register a new schema version and an automated guardrail check (diff-based) that flags potential downstream breakages.
Per-tenant metrics: validation_success_count, validation_failure_count, transformed_count, deadletter_rate are available in the Console within Runtime > Observability > Ingest Gateway.
Canary mode available: tenants can opt into strict validation; rollout plan documented and tested with two tenants in staging.
Migration playbook documented (Confluence) with steps for model teams to rename labels, add defaults, or request a new schema version.
Integration tests cover: rename mapping, optional label addition, numeric-string coercion, rejected breaking change in strict mode, and dead-letter forwarding.
Performance regression: gateway adds <1.5ms P95 latency at target load (1000 rps per node) in standard mode and <3ms in strict mode.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: strict gating can cause silent metric loss for tenants that upgrade infra faster than schema. Mitigation: default to permissive passthrough + tagging; provide immediate telemetry and a dashboard showing 'unvalidated' traffic. Risk: added CPU/latency on ingest path. Mitigation: implement fast-path cache for common schema versions and perform validation in a hot loop native module where possible.
implementation_plan: 1) Schema registry service + initial schemas import (2 weeks). 2) Lightweight gateway filter & normalization engine (3 weeks). 3) Integration tests, CI, and perf benchmarking (1 week). 4) Staged rollout: internal tenants -> two external canaries -> global. 5) Dashboarding and alerts (parallel).
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboards: 'Ingest Gateway - Validation' and 'Ingest Gateway - Latency'. Alerts: validation_failure_rate > 0.5% sustained for 15m (pager for infra), deadletter_volume spike > 3x baseline (pager). Add SLO for gateway P95 latency as part of runtime-1.19 objectives.
